verdict: One Facebook lead campaign ran this period at $2,330 spend with no lead data connected to measure results.
diagnosis: Spend collapsed from a $13.63 daily average to $3.85 on the latest day, suggesting the PCOS and Postpartum campaign is winding down or capped.

signals.headline: $2,330 spent on one campaign
signals.detail: All 28-day paid budget flowed to the PCOS and Postpartum persona lead campaign on Facebook. No diversification this period.

signals.headline: Daily spend dropped to $3.85
signals.detail: Latest day is 72% below the 28-day average of $13.63. Campaign is throttling down or hitting delivery limits.

signals.headline: 0 lead or booking data connected
signals.detail: No customer relationship data, no local presence data, no organic data. Impossible to judge if the $2,330 produced members.

signals.headline: 346,446 impressions delivered
signals.detail: Reach is healthy for a single-persona campaign. The question is whether that audience actually filled out the lead form.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.body: Premium and boutique fitness studios typically see Facebook lead costs of $25 to $50, versus $8–$15 for budget gyms. Fitness lead-form conversion sits near 14%, the highest of any industry.

seasonal.label: Seasonal
seasonal.body: September 2025 was the year's peak lead cost for fitness at roughly $60, running about 25% above the global baseline. Back-to-school demand typically pushes fitness advertising costs up this month.

competitor.label: Category
competitor.body: Boutique studios in 2026 are pulling budget away from acquisition and into retention, community, and personalized programming. Rising rent and marketing costs are squeezing margins across the category.

recommendations.title: Connect lead tracking before the next spend cycle
recommendations.detail: Without booking or lead data flowing in, the $2,330 is a black box. Consider wiring Facebook lead forms to your booking or customer system this week.

recommendations.title: Confirm whether the campaign should keep running
recommendations.detail: Daily spend fell to $3.85. Worth checking if this is intentional pacing, a budget cap, or ad fatigue on the PCOS and Postpartum creative.

recommendations.title: Test a second persona or offer angle
recommendations.detail: One campaign, one audience is fragile. Consider testing a second angle, such as beginner Pilates or postnatal strength, to compare cost per lead.
